newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom share sale to start May 6.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom share sale to start May 6.

text.p: The French government will sell between 30 and 50 billion francs of shares in telecommunications operator France Telecom SA on May 6 and trading in the stock will start in Paris and New York on June 9, company chairman Michel Bon said on Wednesday.
The partial privatisation of France Telecom could be the biggest market float in France since the privatisation of oil group Elf-Aquitaine in February 1994 which raised 35.7 billion francs.

France Telecom also reported a 1996 net attributable profit of 2.1 billion francs ($371.7 million), down from 9.2 billion for 1995. On a proforma basis, excluding exceptional charges, it recorded a net profit of 14.5 billion compared with 14 billion in 1995.
France Telecom, the former state telecoms monopoly, will face full competition in France and the rest of Europe in 1998 when the market will be fully liberalised.

It has teamed up with Germany's Deutsche Telekom in the Atlas alliance to service international business clients, and the two groups concluded the Global One alliance with Sprint Corp of the United States and hold a joint 20 percent stake in Sprint. ($ = 5.65 French Francs)
